matched_prompt: Show that the function x ↦ x^2 is continuous on ℝ.
openmath_xml: <OMOBJ xmlns="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><OMA><OMS cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" cd="pals1" name="continuous_on"/><OMS cd="setname1" name="R"/><OMBIND><OMS cd="fns1" name="lambda"/><OMBVAR><OMV name="x"/></OMBVAR><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="power"/><OMV name="x"/><OMI>2</OMI></OMA></OMBIND></OMA></OMOBJ>
proof_strategy: Use `Metric.continuous_iff` and an explicit epsilon-delta proof. For ε > 0 at x, choose δ = min 1 (ε / (2 * |x| + 1)); then bound `|y ^ 2 - x ^ 2| = |y - x| * |y + x|`. Do not close the proof with shortcut continuity lemmas such as `continuous_id.pow`.
sketch_steps: Rewrite continuity using `Metric.continuous_iff`.
Fix x and ε > 0.
Choose δ = min 1 (ε / (2 * |x| + 1)).
Use |y - x| < 1 to show |y + x| ≤ 2 * |x| + 1.
Conclude |y^2 - x^2| = |y - x| * |y + x| < ε.

proof_strategy: Generalize the square-function continuity draft by induction on the natural exponent. The base case is constant. In the successor case, use the epsilon-delta product estimate with a local bound for x^n and the induction hypothesis; do not replace the target with the x^2 theorem.

Relate the problem to the `continuous_square` draft as the same polynomial/Power continuity family.
Prove by induction on n and expand the successor product step with an epsilon split and a local factor bound.
Do not instantiate n = 2 or reuse the `pals_continuous_square` formal statement.
Conclude the successor case with the same local bounding idea as the square proof.

proof_strategy: Use `Metric.continuous_iff`. At a point x and tolerance ε > 0, split on a = 0. If a = 0, the output distance is zero and any positive δ works. If a ≠ 0, choose δ = ε / |a|; then `|(a*y+b) - (a*x+b)| = |a| * |y-x| < ε`. Do not replace the requested argument with `continuous_const.mul continuous_id`.
sketch_steps: setup: Rewrite continuity with `Metric.continuous_iff`, then fix x and ε > 0.
case_split: Separate the constant case a = 0 from a ≠ 0.
derive: For a ≠ 0 choose δ = ε / |a| and prove δ > 0.
calculation: Cancel b and factor the difference as |a| * |y - x|.
conclude: Multiply the δ-bound by |a| to obtain an output distance below ε.

proof_strategy: Use `Metric.continuous_iff` and choose δ = ε. Apply the reverse triangle inequality `||y| - |x|| ≤ |y - x|`; therefore an input distance below δ is already an output distance below ε. Avoid closing immediately with `continuous_abs`.

derive: Choose δ = ε, whose positivity is exactly the assumption on ε.
calculation: Rewrite the output distance as ||y| - |x||.
apply_theorem: Use `abs_sub_abs_le_abs_sub` to bound it by |y - x|.
conclude: Combine the reverse-triangle bound with dist y x < δ = ε.

proof_strategy: At a fixed x ≠ 0 and ε > 0, first keep y away from zero by requiring |y - x| < |x| / 2, which gives |y| ≥ |x| / 2. Also require |y - x| < ε * |x|^2 / 2. Choose δ as the minimum of those positive bounds. Then use `|1/y - 1/x| = |y-x| / (|x|*|y|)` and the lower bound on |y|. Do not replace the requested argument with `continuousAt_inv₀`.
sketch_steps: setup: Fix x in ℝ \ {0} and ε > 0; first prove continuity at x.
derive: Choose δ = min (|x| / 2) (ε * |x|^2 / 2) and prove δ > 0.
derive: From |y - x| < |x| / 2, prove |y| ≥ |x| / 2 and hence y ≠ 0.
calculation: Rewrite |y⁻¹ - x⁻¹| as |y - x| / (|x| * |y|).
conclude: Obtain continuity at x, then restrict it to `ContinuousWithinAt` on ℝ \ {0}.

proof_strategy: Factor (y+1)^2-(x+1)^2 and bound |y+x+2| on a unit neighborhood.
sketch_steps: setup: Fix a base point x and a tolerance ε > 0.
derive: Restrict to |y - x| < 1 so every variable factor has an explicit local bound.
calculation: Factor the difference and set C = 2|x|+3 for |y+x+2|.
apply_theorem: Choose δ = min(1, ε/C); C is positive and bounds |y+x+2|.
conclude: Substitute |y - x| < δ into the estimate to obtain output distance < ε.

matched_prompt: Show that the function x ↦ |x-1| is continuous on ℝ.
openmath_xml: <OMOBJ xmlns="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><OMA><OMS cd="pals1" name="continuous_on" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" /><OMS cd="setname1" name="R" /><OMBIND><OMS cd="fns1" name="lambda" /><OMBVAR><OMV name="x" /></OMBVAR><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="abs" /><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="minus" /><OMV name="x" /><OMI>1</OMI></OMA></OMA></OMBIND></OMA></OMOBJ>
proof_strategy: Choose δ = ε and apply the reverse triangle inequality after translation.
sketch_steps: setup: Fix a base point x and a tolerance ε > 0.
derive: Choose δ = ε.
calculation: Bound ||y-1|-|x-1|| by |(y-1)-(x-1)| = |y-x|.
apply_theorem: Choose δ = ε.
conclude: Substitute |y - x| < δ into the estimate to obtain output distance < ε.

matched_prompt: Show that the function x ↦ |2*x+1| is continuous on ℝ.

proof_strategy: Choose δ = ε/2; reverse triangle inequality reduces the output change to 2|y-x|.
sketch_steps: setup: Fix a base point x and a tolerance ε > 0.
derive: Choose δ = ε/2.
calculation: Bound the absolute-value difference by |(2y+1)-(2x+1)| = 2|y-x|.
apply_theorem: Choose δ = ε/2, which is positive.
conclude: Substitute |y - x| < δ into the estimate to obtain output distance < ε.

matched_prompt: Show that the identity function x ↦ x is continuous on ℝ.
openmath_xml: <OMOBJ xmlns="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><OMA><OMS cd="pals1" name="continuous_on" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" /><OMS cd="setname1" name="R" /><OMBIND><OMS cd="fns1" name="lambda" /><OMBVAR><OMV name="x" /></OMBVAR><OMV name="x" /></OMBIND></OMA></OMOBJ>
proof_strategy: Choose δ = ε because the identity function preserves the input distance exactly.
sketch_steps: setup: Fix a base point x and a tolerance ε > 0.
derive: Choose δ = ε, which is positive.
calculation: The output distance is |y - x|.
apply_theorem: Apply the hypothesis |y - x| < δ = ε directly.
conclude: This choice works at every x, so the identity function is continuous.

matched_prompt: Show that the function x ↦ |x^2-1| is continuous on ℝ.
openmath_xml: <OMOBJ xmlns="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><OMA><OMS cd="pals1" name="continuous_on" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" /><OMS cd="setname1" name="R" /><OMBIND><OMS cd="fns1" name="lambda" /><OMBVAR><OMV name="x" /></OMBVAR><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="abs" /><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="minus" /><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="power" /><OMV name="x" /><OMI>2</OMI></OMA><OMI>1</OMI></OMA></OMA></OMBIND></OMA></OMOBJ>
proof_strategy: Apply reverse triangle inequality, cancel the constants, and use the local difference-of-squares estimate.
sketch_steps: setup: Fix a base point x and a tolerance ε > 0.
derive: Restrict to |y - x| < 1 so every variable factor has an explicit local bound.
calculation: Bound by |y-x||y+x| and set C = 2|x|+1.
apply_theorem: Choose δ = min(1, ε/C); C is positive and bounds |y+x|.
conclude: Substitute |y - x| < δ into the estimate to obtain output distance < ε.

proof_strategy: Use x^2+1 ≥ 1, combine the fractions, and locally bound the polynomial numerator of the difference before choosing δ.
sketch_steps: setup: Fix a base point x and a tolerance ε > 0.
derive: Restrict to |y - x| < 1 so every variable factor has an explicit local bound.
calculation: Factor by y-x and set C = 1+|x|(|x|+1); denominators are at least 1.
apply_theorem: Choose δ = min(1, ε/C); C is positive and bounds the quotient coefficient.
conclude: Substitute |y - x| < δ into the estimate to obtain output distance < ε.

derive: Restrict to |y - x| < 1 so every variable factor has an explicit local bound.

apply_theorem: Choose δ = min(1, ε/C); C is positive and denominators are at least 1.

proof_strategy: Use denominator lower bounds, combine fractions, factor the numerator difference by y-x, and bound remaining factors locally.
sketch_steps: setup: Fix a base point x and a tolerance ε > 0.
derive: Restrict to |y - x| < 1 so every variable factor has an explicit local bound.
calculation: Factor as (y-x)(1-xy-x-y) and set C = |x|^2+3|x|+2.
apply_theorem: Choose δ = min(1, ε/C); C is positive and denominators are at least 1.
conclude: Substitute |y - x| < δ into the estimate to obtain output distance < ε.

matched_prompt: Show that the function x ↦ (x^2-1)/(x^2+1) is continuous on ℝ.
openmath_xml: <OMOBJ xmlns="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><OMA><OMS cd="pals1" name="continuous_on" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" /><OMS cd="setname1" name="R" /><OMBIND><OMS cd="fns1" name="lambda" /><OMBVAR><OMV name="x" /></OMBVAR><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="divide" /><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="minus" /><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="power" /><OMV name="x" /><OMI>2</OMI></OMA><OMI>1</OMI></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="plus" /><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="power" /><OMV name="x" /><OMI>2</OMI></OMA><OMI>1</OMI></OMA></OMA></OMBIND></OMA></OMOBJ>
proof_strategy: Use denominators ≥ 1; after combining fractions the numerator is a constant multiple of y^2-x^2, which has a local epsilon-delta bound.
sketch_steps: setup: Fix a base point x and a tolerance ε > 0.
derive: Restrict to |y - x| < 1 so every variable factor has an explicit local bound.
calculation: Simplify to 2|y-x||y+x| over denominators at least 1 and set C = 2(2|x|+1).
apply_theorem: Choose δ = min(1, ε/C); C is positive and bounds the quotient coefficient.
conclude: Substitute |y - x| < δ into the estimate to obtain output distance < ε.
